title: stdlib Deep Dive & pip
subtitle: json, datetime, pathlib, requests, venv, and pip
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Real-world Python programs need to work with dates, parse JSON APIs, find files, make HTTP requests, and install third-party packages. The tools for all of this exist — you just need to know where.
whyItExists.solution: The Python standard library covers most daily needs. For the rest (like HTTP requests), PyPI has 500,000+ packages installable with pip. Virtual environments isolate project dependencies.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Whenever you need to interact with the outside world: APIs, files, time, the network.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't pip install a 50MB framework for a task the stdlib handles. Don't skip virtual environments — dependency conflicts are painful to debug.

explainModes.beginner: Python comes with batteries included — a huge library of ready-made modules. When you need something it doesn't have (like making web requests), you install it with pip. Virtual environments keep each project's packages separate so they don't conflict.
explainModes.simple: json.dumps/loads: dict ↔ JSON string. json.dump/load: dict ↔ JSON file. datetime.now(), timedelta for date math. pathlib.Path for file system operations. requests.get/post for HTTP (install: pip install requests). python -m venv venv to create a virtual env. pip install package, pip freeze > requirements.txt, pip install -r requirements.txt.
explainModes.standard: json handles None→null, True→true, False→false. datetime is naive (no timezone) by default — use datetime.timezone.utc or the third-party 'zoneinfo' module. pathlib.Path works across Windows/Linux/Mac. requests returns a Response: .status_code, .json(), .text, .raise_for_status(). Virtual envs live in a folder (venv/ by default) — never commit to git.
explainModes.technical: json.dumps has indent, separators, default (for custom serialization), sort_keys. datetime.fromisoformat() parses ISO 8601 (Python 3.7+). datetime.strptime/strftime for custom formats. pathlib.Path.open() returns a file object — preferred over open() with a string path. requests.Session() for connection pooling and shared headers. pip install -e . for editable installs (src layout). pyproject.toml is the modern packaging config.
explainModes.deepDive: json.JSONEncoder subclass with default() method for custom types. dateutil.parser for fuzzy date parsing (third-party). httpx as a modern async-capable alternative to requests. uv as a fast modern pip alternative. PEP 517/518 — pyproject.toml-based builds. importlib.metadata for reading installed package metadata. pip-tools / poetry / pdm for advanced dependency management.

content.text: json — working with APIs and config

content.code:
import json

# Python dict → JSON string
data = {
    'name': 'Prashant',
    'scores': [95, 82, 78],
    'active': True,
    'email': None
}

json_str = json.dumps(data)           # compact
json_pretty = json.dumps(data, indent=2)  # readable
print(json_pretty)
# {
#   "name": "Prashant",
#   "scores": [95, 82, 78],
#   "active": true,
#   "email": null
# }

# JSON string → Python dict
parsed = json.loads(json_str)
print(parsed['name'])   # Prashant
print(type(parsed['active']))   # <class 'bool'>

# Read/write JSON files
with open('data.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)     # write

with open('data.json') as f:
    loaded = json.load(f)            # read

# Type mappings
# Python  →  JSON
# dict    →  object {}
# list    →  array  []
# str     →  string ""
# int     →  number
# float   →  number
# True    →  true
# False   →  false
# None    →  null

content.text: datetime — working with dates and times

content.code:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, date

# Current date and time
now = datetime.now()
print(now)                      # 2026-09-20 14:30:00.123456
print(now.year, now.month, now.day)
print(now.hour, now.minute, now.second)

# Date arithmetic
tomorrow = now + timedelta(days=1)
last_week = now - timedelta(weeks=1)
print(tomorrow.date())          # 2026-09-21
print(last_week.date())         # 2026-09-13

# Format: datetime → string
formatted = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')
print(formatted)    # '2026-09-20 14:30'

# Parse: string → datetime
dt = datetime.strptime('20-09-2026', '%d-%m-%Y')
print(dt.year)      # 2026

# ISO format (for APIs)
iso = now.isoformat()           # '2026-09-20T14:30:00.123456'
back = datetime.fromisoformat(iso)   # parse back

# Just a date (no time)
today = date.today()
birthday = date(1998, 6, 15)
age_days = (today - birthday).days
print(f'{age_days} days old')

# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate it
# Windows:
venv\Scripts\activate
# Mac/Linux:
source venv/bin/activate

# Your prompt now shows (venv)
# Install packages
pip install requests
pip install requests==2.31.0     # specific version
pip install "requests>=2.28"     # minimum version

# See what's installed
pip list
pip show requests

# Save dependencies for sharing
pip freeze > requirements.txt    # saves exact versions

# Install from requirements file
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Deactivate when done
deactivate

import requests

# GET request
response = requests.get('https://api.github.com/users/torvalds')

print(response.status_code)     # 200
print(response.headers['content-type'])   # application/json

data = response.json()           # parse JSON response
print(data['name'])              # Linus Torvalds
print(data['public_repos'])      # number of repos

# Error handling
try:
    resp = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data', timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()      # raises HTTPError if 4xx/5xx
    data = resp.json()
except requests.Timeout:
    print('Request timed out')
except requests.HTTPError as e:
    print(f'HTTP Error: {e}')

# POST request with JSON body
payload = {'username': 'prashant', 'email': 'p@example.com'}
resp = requests.post(
    'https://httpbin.org/post',
    json=payload,                # auto-sets Content-Type: application/json
    headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer my-token'}
)
print(resp.status_code)

questions.question: Why should you use a virtual environment for each project?
options: It isolates project dependencies so different projects can use different package versions without conflict
It is required to use pip
questions.explanation: Without virtual environments, all pip packages are installed globally. If Project A needs requests==2.28 and Project B needs requests==2.31, you'll have a conflict. Virtual environments give each project its own isolated package directory.

faq.q: What is the difference between json.dump() and json.dumps()?
faq.a: json.dumps() converts Python → JSON string (in memory). json.dump() writes Python → JSON directly to a file object. The 's' stands for 'string'. Same pattern: json.loads() parses a JSON string, json.load() reads from a file.

faq.q: Do I need to install requests? It's not in the standard library?
faq.a: Correct — requests is a third-party package. Install with: pip install requests. Python 3.11+ includes urllib.request in stdlib, but requests is far more ergonomic. Python 3.12's httpx is another modern option.
